# Volume clock — 13:00 volume acceleration, overnight TQQQ

**Development window only:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29. The 2024-2026 holdout
was not used in this analysis; the lead owns the one-shot holdout.

**Verdict (short):** a dev-only family candidate that **clears the TQQQ dev
bar at 1 bp on all three axes** — 37.25% CAGR, 21.87% max drawdown, 1.49
Sharpe, 594 entries / 1,188 fills. The volume-acceleration attribution is
strong and survives volatility controls and placebos. **But the CAGR edge over
TQQQ is only +0.53 pp at 1 bp, and costs erase it at 5 bp (29.32%).** The
durable improvement is risk: drawdown falls from 82.3% to 21.9% and Sharpe
rises from 0.82 to 1.49. The exact 13:00 sampling is a tuned choice and is the
main overfit risk. This is not a holdout claim.

---

## 1. Rules and decision clock

The strategy is an overnight TQQQ position gated by a **volume-acceleration
state** measured at 13:00 ET:

```
accel_k = sum(QQQ volume, 12:31..13:00, session k)
          --------------------------------------------------
          median over sessions k-20..k-1 of the same 30-minute sum
```

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Decision clock | close of the 13:00 ET bar (offset 210 from 09:30); fill at 13:01 open |
| Volume window | 12:31-13:00 ET (30 one-minute QQQ bars) |
| Normalisation | prior-20 same-time-of-day median; strictly before session k |
| State | enter overnight long if `accel < 0.75`; exit if `accel > 0.85`; otherwise hold prior state (deadband) |
| Position | 100% TQQQ at 13:01, hold through 15:59, sell at next 09:30 open; cash otherwise |
| Costs / fills | next-open fills, 2% band, 1 bp headline plus 5/10 bp |
| Constraints | long only, weights ≥ 0, row sum ≤ 1 |

No daily trend SMA, volatility targeting, drawdown/capitulation event,
calendar window, opening range, closing-auction/rebalance-flow signal, or ML
classifier. The 13:00 clock is an intraday sampling time for the volume state,
not a day-level calendar rule. The BIL-flat variant is reported separately;
the headline uses cash because the BIL leg doubles the traded legs in the
shared simulator and is much more cost-sensitive.

## 2. Headline development result

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover | Ending equity |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 bp | 39.31% | 21.48% | 1.56 | 2.53 | 23.07% | 13.6% | 1,188 | 4,945x | $1,410,995 |
| **1 bp** | **37.25%** | **21.87%** | **1.49** | **2.41** | **23.05%** | **13.6%** | **1,188** | **4,534x** | **$1,252,943** |
| 5 bp | 29.32% | 23.42% | 1.24 | 1.98 | 23.00% | 13.6% | 1,188 | 3,233x | $779,031 |
| 10 bp | 20.05% | 36.05% | 0.91 | 1.44 | 22.96% | 13.6% | 1,188 | 2,164x | $430,114 |

Daily-close marks (comparable to the task bar): **37.25% CAGR, 20.84% max DD,
1.47 Sharpe.** The task bar is 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% DD / 0.82 Sharpe. The
1 bp result clears all three, but the CAGR margin is 0.53 pp; at 5 bp the
strategy is below the bar on CAGR and above it on DD/Sharpe.

### Benchmarks (same harness)

| Asset | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Vol |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 66.55% |
| QQQ | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 | 22.02% |
| BIL | 1.39% | 0.24% | 0.92 | 1.52% |

The brief's official TQQQ dev bar is 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82; the harness
buy-and-hold is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80. The difference is daily-close versus
1-minute marking and is within rounding of the bar.

### BIL-flat variant

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Fills | Turnover | Ending equity |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 36.68% | 22.28% | 1.47 | 2.38 | 2,377 | 8,687x | $1,211,731 |
| 5 bp | 21.33% | 34.81% | 0.96 | 1.51 | 2,377 | 4,496x | $468,251 |
| 10 bp | 4.55% | 57.17% | 0.31 | 0.47 | 2,377 | 2,179x | $142,666 |

BIL at 1 bp is 0.04 pp below the TQQQ CAGR bar and is essentially tied; at
5/10 bp it is materially worse than cash because every TQQQ entry/exit also
trades the BIL leg. The neutral state is therefore implemented as cash in the
headline; the BIL state is available and reported.

## 3. Activity

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Entries (TQQQ buys) | 594 |
| Fills (buys + sells) | 1,188 |
| Entries per year | 74.4 |
| Average holding period | 29.8 h (median 20.5 h, max 92.5 h) |
| TQQQ bar-time exposure | 13.6% |
| Overnight participation | ~29.5% of sessions |
| Turnover at 1 bp | 4,534x |

The activity floor is met with room: 594 entries and 1,188 fills over 8 years.
The median holding period is one overnight (20.5 h); the mean is pulled up by
weekends and holidays. The position is flat during the day.

## 4. Mechanism evidence

At 13:00 the acceleration state splits the overnight distribution sharply:

| Bucket | n | Mean overnight TQQQ | Median | t | Win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `accel < 0.75` | 537 | **+41.4 bp** | +32.4 bp | 4.53 | 58.1% |
| deadband 0.75-0.85 | 193 | -4.0 bp | 0.0 bp | -0.23 | 50.8% |
| `accel > 0.85` | 1,246 | +0.2 bp | +18.9 bp | 0.02 | 56.2% |

Low minus high = **+41.2 bp per night**. The high-acceleration bucket has a
positive median but a near-zero mean: its left tail is the problem. The ten
worst overnight TQQQ returns in the sample all occurred after high-acceleration
days, including 2020-03-13 (-29.1%, accel 1.71), 2020-03-06 (-20.0%, accel
1.39), 2020-03-11 (-19.6%, accel 1.32), 2020-03-17 (-16.2%, accel 1.66), and
2020-09-04 (-11.9%, accel 4.81).

The acceleration effect is not a volatility proxy. Regressing the overnight
return on the `accel < 0.75` dummy, log realised 13:00 volatility, and the
absolute open-to-13:00 return:

| Term | Coefficient | t |
|---|---:|---:|
| constant | -1.7 bp | -0.03 |
| `accel < 0.75` | **+40.4 bp** | **3.07** |
| log realised vol | -1.0 bp | -0.07 |
| abs r_open | -462 bp per unit | -0.40 |

Realised volatility is insignificant once the acceleration state is included.
A double sort also survives: low-accel nights average +20.8 bp in low-vol
buckets and +23.8 bp in high-vol buckets; high-accel nights average +5.3 bp
and -3.8 bp respectively.

### The sign of the volume-weighted move

The secondary hypothesis — that the sign of the volume-weighted price move
predicts the overnight return — has standalone content but does not add to the
acceleration gate:

| Rule | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| VWAP deviation > -10 bp only | 40.40% | 46.29% | 1.08 | 2,758 |
| r_open > -20 bp only | 38.93% | 53.18% | 1.05 | 2,660 |
| `accel < 0.75` and VWAP > -10 bp | 28.31% | 21.21% | 1.43 | 924 |
| **`accel` state only (headline)** | **37.25%** | **21.87%** | **1.49** | **1,188** |

The sign alone earns a similar CAGR but with more than twice the drawdown.
Conditioning on both reduces CAGR to 28.3% while improving Sharpe only
marginally (1.43 vs 1.49). The acceleration state is the primary driver; the
sign is a secondary, correlated confirmation, not an independent edge. This is
reported as a partial result for the sign hypothesis, not a win.

### Volume attribution vs controls

| Control | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All sessions, overnight TQQQ | 10.10% | 76.47% | 0.45 | 3,992 |
| Static `accel < 0.75`, no hysteresis | 36.01% | 21.93% | 1.51 | 1,074 |
| High-acceleration state only | -15.95% | 91.30% | -0.17 | 2,492 |
| TQQQ buy & hold | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1 |

The all-sessions overnight control earns 10.1% CAGR; the acceleration gate
adds 27 pp and cuts drawdown from 76% to 22%. The high-acceleration state
alone loses 16% CAGR. This is not just overnight beta.

## 5. Parameter plateau

### Pre-registered 8-cell grid

| Cell | Entries | 1 bp CAGR | 1 bp DD | 1 bp Sharpe | 5 bp CAGR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12:45, 0.75-0.85 | 634 | 22.20% | 42.67% | 0.93 | 14.68% |
| 13:00, 0.70-0.80 | 510 | 27.42% | 23.88% | 1.27 | 21.07% |
| **13:00, 0.75-0.85 (centre)** | **594** | **37.25%** | **21.87%** | **1.49** | **29.32%** |
| 13:00, 0.75-0.90 | 637 | 32.95% | 25.51% | 1.32 | 24.73% |
| 13:00, 0.80-0.90 | 716 | 35.83% | 32.64% | 1.32 | 26.43% |
| 13:00, 0.80-1.00 | 805 | 33.60% | 42.57% | 1.20 | 23.25% |
| 13:15, 0.75-0.85 | 632 | 25.98% | 27.85% | 1.14 | 18.25% |
| 13:30, 0.75-0.85 | 641 | 12.04% | 52.25% | 0.61 | 5.07% |

All eight cells are positive at 1 bp and 5 bp, so the "at least 6 of 8 positive"
criterion passes. The **threshold** plateau at 13:00 is broad: the five 13:00
cells span 27.4-37.3% CAGR and Sharpe 1.20-1.49. The **time** dimension is a
ridge with a peak, not a flat plateau: 12:45 = 22.2%, 13:00 = 37.3%,
13:15 = 26.0%, 13:30 = 12.0%. The 13:00 cell is 11-15 pp above its nearest time
neighbours. This is the main specification risk and is not hidden.

The broader 20-cell neighbour table (12:00-13:30 × four deadbands) spans
8.9-37.3% CAGR and 0.48-1.49 Sharpe; the 13:00 row is the best row. A 60-minute
window at 13:00 drops to 19.4-22.6% CAGR, a 90-minute composite (12:45/13:00/
13:15) reaches 33.9% CAGR with a 45.4% DD, and 3/5-day smoothing reaches
22.7-27.1%. The 30-minute window is the best expression; smoothing removes the
very urgency the mechanism is trying to measure.

## 6. Subperiods and yearly

| Period | CAGR | Max DD |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 22.39% | 21.87% |
| 2020-2021 | 65.26% | 15.85% |
| 2022-2023 | 43.62% | 20.66% |

All three are positive. The 2020-2021 period dominates, but 2016-2019 and
2022-2023 are not dependent on it: excluding 2020 entirely gives 27.98% CAGR,
20.84% DD, 1.23 Sharpe. Excluding the ten best strategy days gives 22.04% CAGR,
20.84% DD, 1.08 Sharpe. The maximum drawdown is in 2016-03-04 → 2016-07-13
(21.87%), not in 2020, which is a useful sign that the risk control is not just
a COVID filter.

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +3.0% | +19.9% |
| 2017 | +24.6% | +114.5% |
| 2018 | -4.2% | -20.8% |
| 2019 | +82.2% | +148.2% |
| 2020 | +124.1% | +104.1% |
| 2021 | +19.9% | +81.1% |
| 2022 | +60.3% | -79.4% |
| 2023 | +28.0% | +192.0% |

2018 is the only negative calendar year. The strategy gives up a lot of the
strong TQQQ up-years (2017, 2019, 2023) and avoids the 2022 crash; the result
is a much smoother path, not a higher-return path.

## 7. Placebo and randomization

All placebos use the same state machine, thresholds and 1 bp cost.

| Test | Real | Placebo mean | Placebo p95 | Max | p-value |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Circular shift, 200 draws | 37.25% | 2.11% | 17.58% | 34.80% | 0.000 |
| Random nights, 200 draws (594 nights) | 37.25% | 3.53% | 18.39% | 26.40% | 0.000 |
| Random decision time, 100 draws (10:30-15:00) | 37.25% | 16.13% | 26.50% | 32.64% | 0.000 |
| Stale signal (prior session's accel) | 8.63% | — | — | — | retains 23% |

The circular-shift and random-night placebos are decisive: the real CAGR is
above the maximum of 200 draws. The random-time placebo is the honest
time-specificity test: the volume state works at many intraday times (mean
16.1% CAGR), but the 13:00 sampling is in the top 1% (max 32.6% < 37.25%).
The signal is timely: using yesterday's acceleration collapses CAGR to 8.6%
and raises drawdown to 50.2%.

Block bootstrap of daily returns (10-day blocks, 1,000 draws):

| Statistic | 5th pct | Median | 95th pct |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 20.3% | 37.4% | 55.0% |
| Sharpe | 0.91 | 1.47 | 1.94 |
| Max DD | — | 22.6% | 33.4% |

## 8. Correlation with the current family winners

Daily-return correlation, development window:

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | +0.226 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | +0.366 |
| relative-value-tqqq | +0.307 |
| fomc-opex-window | +0.341 |
| family-session-timing | +0.402 |
| family-short-reversal | +0.337 |
| family-rebalance-flow | +0.324 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | +0.305 |
| family-ml-microstructure | +0.314 |
| overnight-drift-filter (not a required winner) | +0.397 |

Range vs the nine required winners: **+0.226 to +0.402**. The strategy is
low-beta to TQQQ (beta 0.138) with a significant daily alpha (10.69 bp/day,
30.9% annualised, t = 3.54) and a 0.399 daily correlation. It is not a clone of
any winner, though it shares the overnight/TQQQ exposure of session-timing and
overnight-drift.

## 9. Causality and implementation

- Truncating the panel at 2022-01-03 and rebuilding the weights reproduces
  every prior weight exactly (`max_abs_diff = 0.0`).
- Truncating mid-session at 2020-03-12 11:07 also reproduces every prior
  weight exactly.
- The 13:00 state uses only sessions k-20..k-1. No full-sample statistic.
- 2,006 of 2,012 sessions have offset 210 exactly at 13:00; six sessions with
  a missing morning bar land at 13:09-13:50, still causal. Half-days with
  fewer than 212 bars are skipped.
- The holdout adapter is the same `build_weights` on the full panel; it uses
  only information available at each 13:00 decision.

## 10. Kill criteria and verdict

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| ≥ 100 fills / ≥ 30 entries | 1,188 fills / 594 entries — pass |
| Volume attribution: low > high, OLS t ≥ 2 | +41.2 bp; t = 3.07 — pass |
| Not a volatility proxy | log-vol t = -0.07; accel t = 3.07 — pass |
| Plateau: ≥ 6 of 8 positive | 8 of 8 positive — pass |
| All three subperiods positive | 22.4% / 65.3% / 43.6% — pass |
| 10 bp CAGR > BIL | 20.05% vs 1.39% — pass |
| Placebo p ≤ 0.10 | 0.000 for circular shift, random nights, random time — pass |
| Stale signal retains < 80% | 23% — pass |
| TQQQ bar at 1 bp | 37.25% / 21.87% / 1.49 vs 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82 — pass |
| BIL variant within 1 pp of bar | 36.68% vs 36.72% — pass (0.04 pp below) |

**Verdict:** accept as a **dev-only family candidate**, with explicit caveats.
The mechanism is real in the development window: a midday volume burst predicts
a bad overnight tail, a volume drought predicts the normal overnight drift, and
the effect survives volatility controls and placebos. The strategy clears the
TQQQ dev bar at 1 bp on CAGR, drawdown and Sharpe, with 594 entries and 1,188
fills. But the CAGR edge is thin (+0.53 pp), it is below the bar at 5 bp
(29.32%), and the exact 13:00 sampling is the strongest cell in a time ridge.
The durable contribution is risk reduction, not return enhancement. The lead's
one-shot 2024-2026 holdout is the arbiter; this report does not claim it will
replicate.

## 11. Limitations

1. **Time specificity.** 13:00 is the peak; 12:45 and 13:15 retain 22-26% CAGR
   and 13:30 falls to 12.0%. The random-time placebo mean is 16.1% CAGR, so the
   volume state is not time-unique, but the exact minute is tuned. A holdout
   failure at 13:00 would not invalidate the volume mechanism, only this
   sampling.
2. **Thin CAGR margin.** 37.25% vs the 36.72% bar is 0.53 pp, well inside
   estimation noise. At 5 bp the CAGR is 29.32%. The honest claim is
   risk-adjusted improvement, not a CAGR win.
3. **BIL implementation.** BIL at 1 bp is 36.68% (0.04 pp below the bar) and
   much worse at 5/10 bp because the shared simulator charges the same
   slippage on the BIL leg. The cash headline is a cost-efficiency choice, not
   a claim that BIL is inferior as an asset.
4. **Overnight gap risk.** The position is 100% TQQQ overnight with no stop.
   The development max drawdown is 21.9%, but a future gap through a stop-free
   overnight could be worse. The 2020 tail is avoided by the state, not by a
   stop.
5. **Concentration in 2020 and a few days.** Ex-2020 CAGR is 28.0%; ex-top-10
   days is 22.0%. The strategy is not a one-year or one-day wonder, but both
   sensitivities are material.
6. **Single market, single asset.** QQQ/TQQQ only. No cross-asset or
   out-of-sample market validation.
7. **Turnover and capacity.** 4,534x at 1 bp; 594 round trips. The 10 bp CAGR
   is 20.05%. Capacity is not modelled.
8. **Data.** QQQ volume is the archive's consolidated share volume, not a full
   TAQ tape; odd-lot/off-exchange detail is absent. Six sessions have a
   missing morning bar; half-days are skipped.
9. **No holdout.** Every number here is development-window. The 2024-2026
   result is unknown and must be run once by the lead.

| File | Contents |

| `HYPOTHESIS.md` | pre-registration, mechanism, rules, falsifiers |
| `strategy.py` | runnable strategy and `result.json` generator |
| `result.json` | headline, grid, neighbours, controls, correlations, causality |
| `robustness.py` | placebo, bootstrap and ex-year tests |

$env:BT_THREADS = "1"

hypothesis_md:
# HYPOTHESIS — family-volume-clock (midday volume acceleration)

**Status:** frozen pre-registration for the confirmatory run.
**Window:** development only, 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29. The 2024-2026 holdout
is not loaded into any analysis and is left for the lead's one-shot run.
**New code:** `strategy.py` (this directory). `robustness.py` runs the placebos.

---

## 1. Mechanism

Market time is not calendar time. The information content of a price move
depends on how much volume has been traded, and on whether volume is arriving
faster or slower than its normal same-time-of-day pace. The family tests a
**volume-acceleration state**, not a price-range, opening-range, closing-flow,
trend, volatility or calendar state.

At 13:00 ET, compare the last 30 minutes of QQQ volume with the same 30-minute
window on each of the prior 20 sessions:

```
accel_k = sum(QQQ volume, 12:31..13:00, session k)
          --------------------------------------------------
          median over k-20..k-1 of the same 30-minute sum
```

`accel` is a pure volume-clock state: it says whether the midday tape is
running hot relative to its own time-of-day norm. The economic claim:

- **Volume burst** (`accel` high): urgent, information-driven repricing.
  Liquidity is being consumed, the move is already widely observed, and the
  overnight tail risk is elevated. Do not hold TQQQ overnight.
- **Volume drought** (`accel` low): no urgent flow. The residual overnight
  drift in TQQQ persists; the absence of a burst is the continuation state.
- **Deadband** (0.75 ≤ accel ≤ 0.85): the state is ambiguous; keep the prior
  state rather than churn.

The sign of the volume-weighted price move is a **secondary** test. At the
same 13:00 decision we compute

```
vwap_dev_k = QQQ close(13:00) / VWAP(09:30..13:00) - 1
```

and test whether the sign of this volume-weighted move predicts the overnight
return, alone and conditional on `accel`. The headline rule uses `accel` only;
the sign is reported as attribution, not silently folded into the centre.

Why 13:00? It is the natural midday sampling point: the opening flow has
settled and the closing flow has not started. The 12:31-13:00 window is
therefore a clean read on whether the middle of the session is urgent. It is
not a day-level calendar window (no month-end, FOMC, opex, holiday, or
turn-of-month rule).

## 2. Exact rules

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Universe | QQQ (volume state), TQQQ (position), cash (idle); BIL variant reported |
| Decision clock | close of the 13:00 ET bar (offset 210 from 09:30) |
| Volume window | 12:31-13:00 ET, 30 one-minute QQQ bars |
| Normalisation | median of the same 30-minute window over the prior 20 sessions, strictly before session k |
| State machine | state 0→1 if `accel < 0.75`; state 1→0 if `accel > 0.85`; otherwise hold |
| Position | state 1: 100% TQQQ at the 13:01 open, hold through the 15:59 close, sell at the next 09:30 open. State 0: cash (0%) |
| Holding | one overnight per entry; no intraday-only leg in the headline |
| Fills | next-minute open, 2% band, 1 bp headline plus 5 bp and 10 bp |
| Constraints | long only, weights ≥ 0, row sum ≤ 1 |
| Not used | daily trend SMA, volatility targeting, drawdown/capitulation event, calendar window, opening range, closing-auction/rebalance flow, ML classifier |

The volume ratio uses raw QQQ share volume from the adjusted 1-minute archive.
Volume is not split-adjusted, but QQQ has no split in the window and the ratio
is scale-free. Half-days and sessions with fewer than 212 bars are skipped
(the 13:00 bar does not exist). Six sessions in 2016-2023 have a missing
morning bar, so offset 210 lands at 13:09-13:50; the decision is later than
13:00 but still causal.

## 3. Pre-registered 8-cell plateau

The centre is **13:00 / enter 0.75 / exit 0.85**. The confirmatory grid varies
the time and the deadband; all cells are run at 1 bp and 5 bp.

| # | Decision | Enter | Exit | Purpose |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 12:45 | 0.75 | 0.85 | 15 min earlier |
| 2 | 13:00 | 0.70 | 0.80 | lower state |
| 3 | 13:00 | 0.75 | 0.85 | **centre** |
| 4 | 13:00 | 0.75 | 0.90 | wider deadband |
| 5 | 13:00 | 0.80 | 0.90 | higher state |
| 6 | 13:00 | 0.80 | 1.00 | highest state / widest band |
| 7 | 13:15 | 0.75 | 0.85 | 15 min later |
| 8 | 13:30 | 0.75 | 0.85 | 30 min later |

A broader 5×4 neighbour table (12:00-13:30 × four deadbands) is reported in
`result.json`.

## 4. Falsifiers (kill criteria)

The family is **not accepted** if any of these holds on the development window:

1. **Too thin:** fewer than 100 fills, or fewer than 30 entries.
2. **No volume attribution:** the low-acceleration bucket's mean overnight
   TQQQ return is not above the high-acceleration bucket, or the OLS dummy
   `accel < 0.75` has t < 2.0 controlling for log realised volatility and
   |open-to-13:00 return|.
3. **Volatility proxy:** the acceleration dummy loses significance in that
   same OLS. Volume acceleration must not be a renamed low-vol filter.
4. **No plateau:** fewer than 6 of the 8 grid cells have positive 1 bp CAGR,
   or both time neighbours (12:45 and 13:15) have CAGR below half the centre.
5. **One-episode wonder:** any of 2016-2019, 2020-2021, 2022-2023 has
   non-positive CAGR.
6. **No risk compensation:** 10 bp CAGR ≤ BIL's development CAGR.
7. **Placebo:** the real CAGR is below the 95th percentile of the
   circular-shift or random-night placebo, or either p-value > 0.10.
8. **Stale signal:** using the prior session's acceleration retains ≥ 80% of
   the real CAGR (the signal would not be timely).
9. **Bar:** the 1 bp result fails both the TQQQ CAGR bar (36.72%) and the
   TQQQ Sharpe bar (0.82). Clearing only one is a risk-adjusted improvement,
   not a CAGR win, and must be stated as such.
10. **BIL requirement:** if the brief requires BIL as the idle asset, the BIL
    variant's 1 bp CAGR must not fall more than 1 pp below the TQQQ bar.

## 5. Data and alignment

  forward-filled volume is used in the signal: a missing minute contributes 0
  and the session is skipped if the 13:00 bar is absent.

- State at session k is known at 13:00:59; the TQQQ weight is placed on the

## 1. Rules and decision clock

The strategy is an overnight TQQQ position gated by a **volume-acceleration
state** measured at 13:00 ET:

```
accel_k = sum(QQQ volume, 12:31..13:00, session k)
          --------------------------------------------------
          median over sessions k-20..k-1 of the same 30-minute sum
```

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Decision clock | close of the 13:00 ET bar (offset 210 from 09:30); fill at 13:01 open |
| Volume window | 12:31-13:00 ET (30 one-minute QQQ bars) |
| Normalisation | prior-20 same-time-of-day median; strictly before session k |
| State | enter overnight long if `accel < 0.75`; exit if `accel > 0.85`; otherwise hold prior state (deadband) |
| Position | 100% TQQQ at 13:01, hold through 15:59, sell at next 09:30 open; cash otherwise |
| Costs / fills | next-open fills, 2% band, 1 bp headline plus 5/10 bp |
| Constraints | long only, weights ≥ 0, row sum ≤ 1 |

No daily trend SMA, volatility targeting, drawdown/capitulation event,
calendar window, opening range, closing-auction/rebalance-flow signal, or ML
classifier. The 13:00 clock is an intraday sampling time for the volume state,
not a day-level calendar rule. The BIL-flat variant is reported separately;
the headline uses cash because the BIL leg doubles the traded legs in the
shared simulator and is much more cost-sensitive.

## 4. Mechanism evidence

At 13:00 the acceleration state splits the overnight distribution sharply:

| Bucket | n | Mean overnight TQQQ | Median | t | Win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `accel < 0.75` | 537 | **+41.4 bp** | +32.4 bp | 4.53 | 58.1% |
| deadband 0.75-0.85 | 193 | -4.0 bp | 0.0 bp | -0.23 | 50.8% |
| `accel > 0.85` | 1,246 | +0.2 bp | +18.9 bp | 0.02 | 56.2% |

Low minus high = **+41.2 bp per night**. The high-acceleration bucket has a
positive median but a near-zero mean: its left tail is the problem. The ten
worst overnight TQQQ returns in the sample all occurred after high-acceleration
days, including 2020-03-13 (-29.1%, accel 1.71), 2020-03-06 (-20.0%, accel
1.39), 2020-03-11 (-19.6%, accel 1.32), 2020-03-17 (-16.2%, accel 1.66), and
2020-09-04 (-11.9%, accel 4.81).

The acceleration effect is not a volatility proxy. Regressing the overnight
return on the `accel < 0.75` dummy, log realised 13:00 volatility, and the
absolute open-to-13:00 return:

| Term | Coefficient | t |
|---|---:|---:|
| constant | -1.7 bp | -0.03 |
| `accel < 0.75` | **+40.4 bp** | **3.07** |
| log realised vol | -1.0 bp | -0.07 |
| abs r_open | -462 bp per unit | -0.40 |

Realised volatility is insignificant once the acceleration state is included.
A double sort also survives: low-accel nights average +20.8 bp in low-vol
buckets and +23.8 bp in high-vol buckets; high-accel nights average +5.3 bp
and -3.8 bp respectively.

### The sign of the volume-weighted move

The secondary hypothesis — that the sign of the volume-weighted price move
predicts the overnight return — has standalone content but does not add to the
acceleration gate:

| Rule | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| VWAP deviation > -10 bp only | 40.40% | 46.29% | 1.08 | 2,758 |
| r_open > -20 bp only | 38.93% | 53.18% | 1.05 | 2,660 |
| `accel < 0.75` and VWAP > -10 bp | 28.31% | 21.21% | 1.43 | 924 |
| **`accel` state only (headline)** | **37.25%** | **21.87%** | **1.49** | **1,188** |

The sign alone earns a similar CAGR but with more than twice the drawdown.
Conditioning on both reduces CAGR to 28.3% while improving Sharpe only
marginally (1.43 vs 1.49). The acceleration state is the primary driver; the
sign is a secondary, correlated confirmation, not an independent edge. This is
reported as a partial result for the sign hypothesis, not a win.

### Volume attribution vs controls

| Control | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All sessions, overnight TQQQ | 10.10% | 76.47% | 0.45 | 3,992 |
| Static `accel < 0.75`, no hysteresis | 36.01% | 21.93% | 1.51 | 1,074 |
| High-acceleration state only | -15.95% | 91.30% | -0.17 | 2,492 |
| TQQQ buy & hold | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1 |

The all-sessions overnight control earns 10.1% CAGR; the acceleration gate
adds 27 pp and cuts drawdown from 76% to 22%. The high-acceleration state
alone loses 16% CAGR. This is not just overnight beta.

"""Volume-clock family: midday volume-acceleration state, overnight TQQQ.

Development window only (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).

Mechanism
---------
The market clock is replaced by a volume clock only for the *state* decision:
at 13:00 ET we compare the last 30 minutes of QQQ volume with the same
30-minute window on each of the prior 20 sessions.  The ratio is a
same-time-of-day volume-acceleration state.

    accel_k = sum(vol[12:31..13:00], session k)
              ------------------------------------
              median over k-20..k-1 of the same 30-minute sum

A volume burst (accel above the exit threshold) marks urgent, information-
driven repricing; the overnight tail risk is elevated.  A volume drought
(accel below the enter threshold) marks the absence of urgent flow; the
residual overnight drift in TQQQ persists.  A hysteresis band between the two
thresholds is the neutral deadband: the prior state is kept.

Rules
-----
* Decision clock: close of the 13:00 ET bar (offset 210 from 09:30).
* Volume window: 12:31-13:00 ET (30 one-minute bars).
* Normalisation: median of the same 30-minute window over the prior 20
  sessions (strictly before session k).  No full-sample statistics.
* State machine:
      state 0 -> 1 if accel < 0.75
      state 1 -> 0 if accel > 0.85
      otherwise state unchanged (deadband).
* If state == 1: buy TQQQ at the 13:01 open, hold through the 15:59 close,
  sell at the next session's 09:30 open.  One overnight per entry.
* If state == 0: cash (0%).  The BIL-flat variant is reported separately;
  under the shared simulator its second leg doubles fills and is much more
  cost-sensitive.
* Long only, weights >= 0, row sum <= 1, 2% band, next-open fills.

The sign of the volume-weighted price move is tested as a secondary signal:
VWAP deviation at 13:00 (close / volume-weighted average price - 1).  It has
standalone predictive content, but combining it with the acceleration gate
lowers CAGR; the acceleration state is the primary driver.  See report.md.

import pandas as pd

import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"

CQ, CT, CB = 0, 1, 2

# Pre-registered centre (frozen before the confirmatory grid).
DEC_MIN = 210      # 13:00 ET bar; signal known at its close
WIN_MIN = 30       # 12:31-13:00 ET
LOOK = 20          # prior-20 same-window median
ENTER = 0.75       # enter the overnight long below this acceleration
EXIT = 0.85        # exit the state above this acceleration
FLAT = "cash"      # headline; "BIL" variant is reported separately

WINNERS = [
    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing", "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow", "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
]
EXTRA_CURVES = ["overnight-drift-filter"]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# data / signal
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def load_panel(start: str = DEV_START, end: str = DEV_END, warmup_days: int = 60):
    """Dev panel plus aligned QQQ share volume."""
    ts, o, c = bt.panel(SYMBOLS, start, end, "1min", warmup_days=warmup_days)
    lo, hi = pd.Timestamp(ts[0]), pd.Timestamp(ts[-1])
    df = bt.load_1m("QQQ")
    df = df[(df["ts"] >= lo) & (df["ts"] <= hi)].set_index("ts").reindex(ts)
    vol = np.nan_to_num(df["volume"].to_numpy(dtype=float), nan=0.0)
    return ts, o, c, vol


def qqq_volume(ts: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> np.ndarray:
    """QQQ share volume aligned to an arbitrary panel index (holdout-safe)."""
    ts = pd.DatetimeIndex(ts)
    lo, hi = pd.Timestamp(ts[0]), pd.Timestamp(ts[-1])
    df = bt.load_1m("QQQ")
    df = df[(df["ts"] >= lo) & (df["ts"] <= hi)].set_index("ts").reindex(ts)
    return np.nan_to_num(df["volume"].to_numpy(dtype=float), nan=0.0)


def volume_acceleration(ts, vol, dec_min: int = DEC_MIN, win: int = WIN_MIN,
                        look: int = LOOK) -> np.ndarray:
    """Same-time-of-day 30-minute volume ratio, strictly causal.

    `accel[k]` uses session k's window ending at `dec_min` and the same window
    on sessions k-look .. k-1.  Sessions with a missing/short window or a zero
    median are NaN.
    """
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    w0 = dec_min - win + 1
    acc = np.full(n, np.nan)
    if w0 < 0:
        return acc
    for k in range(look, n):
        m = min(int(last[k]) - int(first[k]) + 1, 390)
        if dec_min >= m - 1:
            continue
        fk = int(first[k])
        cur = float(np.sum(vol[fk + w0: fk + dec_min + 1]))
        hist = [
            float(np.sum(vol[int(first[kk]) + w0: int(first[kk]) + dec_min + 1]))
            for kk in range(k - look, k)
        ]
        med = float(np.median(hist))
        if med > 0:
            acc[k] = cur / med
    return acc


def state_mask(accel: np.ndarray, enter: float, exit_: float,
               hysteresis: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
    """Overnight-long state from the acceleration series."""
    n = len(accel)
    mask = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    state = 0
    for k in range(n):
        a = accel[k]
        if not np.isfinite(a):
            state = 0
            continue
        if not hysteresis:
            state = 1 if a < enter else 0
        elif state == 0 and a < enter:
            state = 1
        elif state == 1 and a > exit_:
            state = 0
        mask[k] = bool(state)
    return mask


def weights_from_mask(ts, mask: np.ndarray, dec_min: int = DEC_MIN,
                      flat: str = FLAT):
    """Build the (n, 3) matrix: overnight TQQQ on mask days, else flat."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    traded = 0
    for k in range(n - 1):
        if not mask[k]:
            continue
        m = min(int(last[k]) - int(first[k]) + 1, 390)
        if dec_min >= m - 1:
            continue
        fk, lk = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        w[fk + dec_min, CT] = 1.0          # fill at 13:01 open
        w[fk + dec_min + 1: lk + 1, CT] = 1.0
        w[lk, CT] = 0.0                    # fill at next session's open
        traded += 1
    w[-1] = w[-2]
    if flat == "BIL":
        w[:, CB] = 1.0 - w[:, CT]
    return w, traded


def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, dec_min: int = DEC_MIN, enter: float = ENTER,
                  exit_: float = EXIT, win: int = WIN_MIN, look: int = LOOK,
                  flat: str = FLAT, accel: np.ndarray | None = None,
                  hysteresis: bool = True, return_diag: bool = False):
    """Required public API.  Returns an (n, 3) long-only weight matrix.

    The function is generic over the panel range: if the lead calls it on the
    full 2016-2026 panel it uses only information available at each 13:00
    decision (prior 20 sessions), so it is holdout-safe.
    """
    ts = pd.DatetimeIndex(ts)
    opens = np.asarray(opens, dtype=float)
    closes = np.asarray(closes, dtype=float)
    if accel is None:
        vol = qqq_volume(ts)
        accel = volume_acceleration(ts, vol, dec_min, win, look)
    mask = state_mask(accel, enter, exit_, hysteresis=hysteresis)
    w, traded = weights_from_mask(ts, mask, dec_min, flat)
    if return_diag:
        return w, {"accel": accel, "mask": mask, "traded": traded}
    return w


def build_holdout_weights(ts, opens, closes):
    """Optional adapter: identical frozen logic on the full panel."""
    return build_weights(ts, opens, closes)

def pack(s: dict) -> dict:
    keys = ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "sortino", "volatility",
            "exposure", "turnover", "fills", "ending_equity", "years")
    return {k: (int(s[k]) if k == "fills" else float(s[k])) for k in keys}


def run_w(ts, o, c, w, slip: float = 1.0, fill_log: bool = False):
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, w, DEV_START, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip,
               fill_log=fill_log)
    return r, bt.stats(r, BPY)


def daily_returns(res: dict) -> pd.Series:
    s = pd.Series(res["equity"], index=pd.to_datetime(res["ts"]))
    d = s.groupby(s.index.normalize()).last()
    d.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(d.index).tz_localize(None).normalize()
    return d.pct_change().dropna()


def daily_curve(res: dict) -> pd.Series:
    s = pd.Series(res["equity"], index=pd.to_datetime(res["ts"]))
    d = s.groupby(s.index.normalize()).last()
    d.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(d.index).tz_localize(None).normalize()
    return d


def daily_stats(res: dict) -> dict:
    d = daily_curve(res)
    eq = d.to_numpy()
    years = (d.index[-1] - d.index[0]).days / 365.25
    rets = np.diff(eq) / eq[:-1]
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    return {
        "cagr": float((eq[-1] / eq[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
        "max_drawdown": float(-(eq / peak - 1).min()),
        "sharpe": float(rets.mean() / rets.std(ddof=0) * np.sqrt(252)),
        "volatility": float(rets.std(ddof=0) * np.sqrt(252)),
        "days": int(len(d)),
    }


def subperiod(ts, equity, lo: str, hi: str) -> dict | None:
    m = ((ts >= pd.Timestamp(lo, tz="America/New_York"))
         & (ts < pd.Timestamp(hi, tz="America/New_York") + pd.Timedelta(days=1)))
    x, tt = equity[m], ts[m]
    if len(x) < 2:
        return None
    years = (tt[-1] - tt[0]).total_seconds() / (365.25 * 86400)
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(x)
    return {"cagr": float((x[-1] / x[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
            "max_drawdown": float(-(x / peak - 1).min())}


def dd_window(ts, equity) -> dict:
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)
    dd = equity / peak - 1.0
    j = int(np.argmin(dd))
    i = int(np.argmax(equity[: j + 1]))
    return {"peak": str(ts[i])[:10], "trough": str(ts[j])[:10],
            "dd": float(-dd[j])}


def alpha_beta_vs_tqqq(ts, c, res) -> dict:
    sr = daily_returns(res)
    tq = pd.Series(c[:, CT], index=pd.to_datetime(ts))
    tr = tq.groupby(tq.index.normalize()).last().pct_change().dropna()
    tr.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(tr.index).tz_localize(None).normalize()
    j = sr.index.intersection(tr.index)
    sr, tr = sr.loc[j], tr.loc[j]
    beta = float(np.cov(sr, tr, ddof=1)[0, 1] / np.var(tr, ddof=1))
    alpha = float(sr.mean() - beta * tr.mean())
    resid = sr.to_numpy() - alpha - beta * tr.to_numpy()
    se = float(np.std(resid, ddof=2) / np.sqrt(len(sr)))
    return {"beta": beta, "alpha_bp_day": alpha * 1e4,
            "alpha_ann": float((1 + alpha) ** 252 - 1),
            "t_alpha": float(alpha / se) if se > 0 else 0.0,
            "corr": float(sr.corr(tr)), "n": int(len(sr))}


def load_curve(slug: str) -> pd.Series | None:
    p = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
    if not p.exists():
        return None
    d = json.loads(p.read_text())

    s.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(s.index).tz_localize(None).normalize()
    return s.pct_change().dropna()


def corr_table(res) -> dict:
    dr = daily_returns(res)
    out = {}
    for slug in WINNERS + EXTRA_CURVES:
        wr = load_curve(slug)
        if wr is None:
            continue
        j = dr.index.intersection(wr.index)
        out[slug] = {"corr": float(dr.loc[j].corr(wr.loc[j])), "n": int(len(j))}
    return out


def signal_diagnostics(accel, mask, ts, o, c) -> dict:
    """Overnight return split by acceleration state, plus vol controls."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    on = np.full(n, np.nan)
    rv = np.full(n, np.nan)
    rop = np.full(n, np.nan)
    vwd = np.full(n, np.nan)

        v = None  # volume not needed for these diagnostics except VWAP

        rv[k] = float(np.std(rr, ddof=0) * np.sqrt(390))
        rop[k] = cl[DEC_MIN] / o[fk, 0] - 1.0
    return {"overnight": on, "rv": rv, "r_open": rop}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# main

def main():

        _, sb = run_w(ts, o, c, wb, slip=slip)
        out["bil_flat_variant"][f"{int(slip)}bp"] = pack(sb)
        print(f"BIL flat {slip:4.1f}bp  CAGR {sb['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {sb['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {sb['sharpe']:4.2f}  fills {sb['fills']:,}  turnover {sb['turnover']:.0f}")

    # daily-close metrics and subperiods
    out["daily_close"] = {k: v for k, v in daily_stats(res1).items()}
    out["subperiods"] = {
        "2016_2019": subperiod(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
        "2020_2021": subperiod(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], "2020-01-02", "2021-12-31"),
        "2022_2023": subperiod(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], "2022-01-03", "2023-12-29"),
    }
    out["yearly"] = {
        str(k): {"strategy": float(v["strategy"]), "benchmark": float(v["benchmark"])}
        for k, v in bt.yearly(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], c[i0:, CT]).items()
    }
    out["dd_window"] = dd_window(res1["ts"], res1["equity"])
    out["alpha_beta_tqqq"] = alpha_beta_vs_tqqq(ts, c, res1)
    out["corr_winners"] = corr_table(res1)

    # holding period / entries from the fill log
    rlog, _ = run_w(ts, o, c, w, slip=1.0, fill_log=True)
    log = rlog["fills_log"]
    buys = [x for x in log if x["side"] == "buy"]
    sells = [x for x in log if x["side"] == "sell"]
    holds = []
    bi = 0
    for s in sells:
        if bi < len(buys) and buys[bi]["ts"] <= s["ts"]:
            holds.append((s["ts"] - buys[bi]["ts"]).total_seconds() / 3600.0)
            bi += 1
    out["activity"] = {
        "fills": int(s1["fills"]), "buys": len(buys), "sells": len(sells),
        "entries": len(buys),
        "avg_hold_hours": float(np.mean(holds)) if holds else 0.0,
        "median_hold_hours": float(np.median(holds)) if holds else 0.0,
        "tqqq_bar_exposure": float(np.mean(w[:, CT] > 0)),
        "nights_per_year": float(len(buys) / s1["years"]),
        "turnover_1bp": float(s1["turnover"]),
    }
    print(f"activity: {len(buys)} entries, avg hold {out['activity']['avg_hold_hours']:.1f}h, "
          f"median {out['activity']['median_hold_hours']:.1f}h")

    # signal attribution: low vs high acceleration, vol controls
    sd = signal_diagnostics(accel, diag["mask"], ts, o, c)
    on = sd["overnight"]; rv = sd["rv"]; rop = sd["r_open"]
    valid = np.isfinite(on) & np.isfinite(accel) & np.isfinite(rv) & np.isfinite(rop)
    lo = valid & (accel < ENTER)
    hi = valid & (accel > EXIT)
    mid = valid & (accel >= ENTER) & (accel <= EXIT)

    def bucket(m):
        x = on[m]
        return {"n": int(len(x)), "mean_bp": float(x.mean() * 1e4),
                "median_bp": float(np.median(x) * 1e4),
                "t": float(x.mean() / (x.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(x)))) if len(x) > 1 else 0.0,
                "win": float(np.mean(x > 0))}

    out["signal_attribution"] = {
        "low_accel": bucket(lo), "deadband": bucket(mid), "high_accel": bucket(hi),
        "low_minus_high_bp": float((on[lo].mean() - on[hi].mean()) * 1e4),
    }

    # OLS: overnight ~ 1 + low_accel + log(rv) + |r_open|
    y = on[valid]
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(valid.sum()), (accel[valid] < ENTER).astype(float),
                         np.log(rv[valid]), np.abs(rop[valid])])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)
    resid = y - X @ beta
    s2 = float(resid @ resid / (len(y) - X.shape[1]))
    se = np.sqrt(np.diag(s2 * np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)))
    out["signal_attribution"]["ols"] = {
        "dep_var": "overnight TQQQ close-to-next-open",
        "terms": ["const", "accel<0.75", "log_realised_vol", "abs_r_open"],
        "coef_bp": [float(b * 1e4) for b in beta],
        "t": [float(b / s) for b, s in zip(beta, se)],
        "n": int(len(y)),
    }
    print(f"low accel {out['signal_attribution']['low_accel']['mean_bp']:.1f}bp "
          f"(n={out['signal_attribution']['low_accel']['n']}) vs high "
          f"{out['signal_attribution']['high_accel']['mean_bp']:.1f}bp "
          f"(n={out['signal_attribution']['high_accel']['n']})")
    print(f"OLS accel<0.75 t={out['signal_attribution']['ols']['t'][1]:.2f}")

    # ---------------- pre-registered 8-cell plateau -------------------------
    grid_specs = [
        ("12:45 e0.75 x0.85", 195, 0.75, 0.85),
        ("13:00 e0.70 x0.80", 210, 0.70, 0.80),
        ("13:00 e0.75 x0.85 (centre)", 210, 0.75, 0.85),
        ("13:00 e0.75 x0.90", 210, 0.75, 0.90),
        ("13:00 e0.80 x0.90", 210, 0.80, 0.90),
        ("13:00 e0.80 x1.00", 210, 0.80, 1.00),
        ("13:15 e0.75 x0.85", 225, 0.75, 0.85),
        ("13:30 e0.75 x0.85", 240, 0.75, 0.85),
    ]
    acc_cache = {d: volume_acceleration(ts, vol, d, WIN_MIN, LOOK)
                 for d in sorted({x[1] for x in grid_specs})}
    grid = []
    for label, dec, ent, ext in grid_specs:
        wg, dg = build_weights(ts, o, c, dec_min=dec, enter=ent, exit_=ext,
                               accel=acc_cache[dec], return_diag=True)
        row = {"cell": label, "dec_min": dec, "enter": ent, "exit": ext,
               "entries": int(dg["traded"])}
        for slip in (1.0, 5.0):
            _, sg = run_w(ts, o, c, wg, slip=slip)
            row[f"{int(slip)}bp"] = pack(sg)
        grid.append(row)
        g1 = row["1bp"]; g5 = row["5bp"]
        print(f"grid {label:30s} 1bp {g1['cagr']*100:6.2f}%/{g1['max_drawdown']*100:5.1f}% "
              f"Sh {g1['sharpe']:4.2f}  5bp {g5['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  entries {row['entries']}")
    out["grid"] = grid

    # ---------------- broader neighbours ------------------------------------
    neigh = []
    for dec in (180, 195, 210, 225, 240):
        for ent, ext in ((0.70, 0.80), (0.75, 0.85), (0.80, 0.90), (0.75, 0.90)):
            a = acc_cache.get(dec)
            if a is None:
                a = volume_acceleration(ts, vol, dec, WIN_MIN, LOOK)
                acc_cache[dec] = a
            wn, dn = build_weights(ts, o, c, dec_min=dec, enter=ent, exit_=ext,
                                   accel=a, return_diag=True)
            _, sn = run_w(ts, o, c, wn, slip=1.0)
            neigh.append({"dec_min": dec, "enter": ent, "exit": ext,
                          "entries": int(dn["traded"]), **pack(sn)})
    out["neighbours"] = neigh

    # ---------------- controls ----------------------------------------------
    controls = {}
    # 1. all sessions, overnight, no signal
    wall = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    for k in range(n - 1):
        fk, lk = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        wall[fk + DEC_MIN, CT] = 1.0
        wall[fk + DEC_MIN + 1: lk + 1, CT] = 1.0
        wall[lk, CT] = 0.0
    wall[-1] = wall[-2]
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, wall); controls["all_sessions_overnight"] = pack(s)
    # 2. static threshold, no hysteresis
    wst, _ = build_weights(ts, o, c, accel=accel, hysteresis=False,
                           return_diag=True)
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, wst); controls["static_accel_lt_0.75"] = pack(s)
    # 3. high-acceleration state only (the bad side)
    mask_hi = np.isfinite(accel) & (accel > EXIT)
    whi, _ = weights_from_mask(ts, mask_hi, DEC_MIN)
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, whi); controls["high_accel_only"] = pack(s)
    # 4. always long TQQQ
    wb = np.zeros((len(ts), 3)); wb[:, CT] = 1.0
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, wb); controls["buy_hold_tqqq"] = pack(s)
    # 5. VWAP sign only (no acceleration gate)
    vwd = np.full(n, np.nan)
    for k in range(LOOK, n):
        m = min(int(last[k]) - int(first[k]) + 1, 390)
        if DEC_MIN >= m - 1:
            continue
        fk = int(first[k]); cl = c[fk:fk + m, 0]; v = vol[fk:fk + m]
        vw = np.sum(v[:DEC_MIN + 1] * cl[:DEC_MIN + 1]) / max(v[:DEC_MIN + 1].sum(), 1)
        vwd[k] = cl[DEC_MIN] / vw - 1.0
    m_vwd = np.isfinite(vwd) & (vwd > -0.001)
    wv, _ = weights_from_mask(ts, m_vwd, DEC_MIN)
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, wv); controls["vwap_dev_gt_-10bp_only"] = pack(s)
    # 6. 13:00 r_open > -20bp only (price-only control)
    rop = np.full(n, np.nan)
    for k in range(LOOK, n):
        m = min(int(last[k]) - int(first[k]) + 1, 390)
        if DEC_MIN >= m - 1:
            continue
        fk = int(first[k])
        rop[k] = c[fk + DEC_MIN, 0] / o[fk, 0] - 1.0
    m_rop = np.isfinite(rop) & (rop > -0.002)
    wr, _ = weights_from_mask(ts, m_rop, DEC_MIN)
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, wr); controls["r_open_gt_-20bp_only"] = pack(s)
    # 7. acceleration + VWAP sign
    m_both = np.isfinite(accel) & np.isfinite(vwd) & (accel < ENTER) & (vwd > -0.001)
    wbo, _ = weights_from_mask(ts, m_both, DEC_MIN)
    _, s = run_w(ts, o, c, wbo); controls["accel_and_vwap_sign"] = pack(s)
    out["controls"] = controls
    for k, v in controls.items():
        print(f"control {k:34s} CAGR {v['cagr']*100:6.2f}% DD {v['max_drawdown']*100:5.1f}% "
              f"Sh {v['sharpe']:4.2f} fills {v['fills']:,}")

    # ---------------- causality / truncation --------------------------------
    j = bt.start_index(ts, "2022-01-03")
    vol_tr = vol[:j]
    a_tr = volume_acceleration(ts[:j], vol_tr, DEC_MIN, WIN_MIN, LOOK)
    w_tr = build_weights(ts[:j], o[:j], c[:j], accel=a_tr)
    out["causality_day_boundary"] = {
        "truncation_date": "2022-01-03",
        "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_tr[:j], w[:j])),
        "max_abs_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(w_tr[:j] - w[:j]))),
    }
    j2 = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12 11:07")
    n_cmp = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12")
    a_tr2 = volume_acceleration(ts[:j2], vol[:j2], DEC_MIN, WIN_MIN, LOOK)
    w_tr2 = build_weights(ts[:j2], o[:j2], c[:j2], accel=a_tr2)
    out["causality_intraday_cut"] = {
        "truncation_date": "2020-03-12 11:07",
        "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_tr2[:n_cmp], w[:n_cmp])),
        "max_abs_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(w_tr2[:n_cmp] - w[:n_cmp]))),
    }
    print("causality", out["causality_day_boundary"], out["causality_intraday_cut"])

    # ---------------- pass / kill summary -----------------------------------
    g = out["grid"]
    pos_grid = sum(1 for r in g if r["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0)
    out["kill_checks"] = {
        "activity_floor_100_fills": bool(s1["fills"] >= 100),
        "entries_ge_30": bool(len(buys) >= 30),
        "cagr_above_tqqq_bar": bool(s1["cagr"] > 0.3672),
        "sharpe_above_tqqq_bar": bool(s1["sharpe"] > 0.82),
        "dd_below_tqqq_bar": bool(s1["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229),
        "ten_bp_above_bil": bool(out["dev"]["10bp"]["cagr"] > out["benchmarks"]["bil"]["cagr"]),
        "all_subperiods_positive": bool(all(
            v is not None and v["cagr"] > 0 for v in out["subperiods"].values())),
        "grid_positive_cells": int(pos_grid),
        "grid_positive_at_least_6_of_8": bool(pos_grid >= 6),
        "volume_attribution_t_ge_2": bool(out["signal_attribution"]["ols"]["t"][1] >= 2.0),
    }
    out["pass"] = {
        "headline_clears_bar_at_1bp": out["bar_check"]["all_three"],
        "risk_adjusted_improvement": bool(
            s1["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229 and s1["sharpe"] > 0.82),
        "cagr_edge_over_bar_pp": float((s1["cagr"] - 0.3672) * 100),
        "note": "CAGR edge at 1bp is small; the durable improvement is drawdown "
                "and Sharpe. At 5bp the CAGR is below the TQQQ bar.",
    }

    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float),
                                      encoding="utf-8")
    print("wrote", HERE / "result.json")
